compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate
(`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that
projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase`
(`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and
`process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds,
at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function
that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline
at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states
the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and
`_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22`
is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus
`_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker:
`_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the
extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the
cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level
name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [ ] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [ ] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
